title: The n×n attention score matrix and its memory footprint
why: Shows the quadratic score matrix dimensions and how one head-layer's fp16 matrix compares to on-chip SRAM and the engine's unified memory.
notes: Axes are token i (rows) and token j (columns); each cell is a dot product of length d=128. Label n=130,659, n²=1.707×10^10 entries, score computation 2.185×10^12 multiply-adds per head per layer, and value aggregation the same again. Memory bar: 1.707×10^10 entries × 2 bytes = 34.1 GB for one head in one layer; compare to SRAM in tens of MB (roughly a thousand times smaller) and to 111.5 GB unified memory (34.1/111.5 = 30.6%). | No axes; this is a dataflow/memory-layout diagram. Left path: standard attention materializes the n² score matrix in HBM and moves it through a 273 GB/s LPDDR5X bus for softmax and value multiply. Right path: Flash Attention loads Q/K tiles into SRAM, computes tile scores, updates m, l, and O with the rescale factor exp(m_old − m_new), and writes only the output; the n² matrix never exists in HBM. Label structural constants and chapter quantities: n², 273 GB/s, initial m = −∞, l = 0, example tile scores [2,4] then [6,8], running m = 4 then 8, running l = 1.135 then 1.156. | Log-log axes: x = sequence length n, y = cost (score entries for quadratic/sparse, operations for linear). Quadratic curve rises as n^2; windowed sparse is linear with constant 4,096; linear attention is linear with d=128. Label n=130,659 with quadratic 1.707×10^10 entries, windowed 5.35×10^8 entries (32-fold reduction), linear 2.14×10^9 operations vs quadratic 2.185×10^12 operations (thousand-fold). Mark linear/quadratic crossover at n=128 for d=128. All quantities are from the chapter. | Axes: asymptotic cost (quadratic vs linear in sequence length n) against exact recall/quality. Exact attention stays exact; sparse, linear and state-space families trade exactness or recall for better asymptotics. S4 uses a fixed-size state; Mamba makes A_t, B_t, C_t input-dependent but still cannot recover exact recall. KV cache is a separate linear memory cost: 921.6 bytes per position across all layers; raising the pool from 262,144 to 1,048,576 positions adds 786,432 × 921.6 bytes = 724.8 MB = 0.675 GiB, rounded to 0.68 GiB per rank. Quadratic cost remains in prefill compute. | Left panel is a dataflow: prompt prefix -> hash -> radix-tree lookup -> reuse cached KV blocks instead of recomputing. Right panel is a memory layout: per-layer KV cache has 2 × n × d values; at n = 130,659 and d = 128 that is 33.4 million values per layer, or 66.9 MB in fp16 per layer. The 262,144-position pool is shared across four streams, giving 32,750 tokens per stream after reply budget and overhead; the native window is 1,048,576 positions, and closing the gap costs 0.68 GiB per rank. Label the sampled cache hit rate 95.9% = 12,285,952 / 12,804,579 and the 313 seconds of avoided prefill at 39,237 tokens/s.
